incidents.vector: Voice-phishing and social engineering impersonating IT support to gain unauthorized access to cloud platforms.
incidents.impact: Names, dates of birth, addresses and Social Security numbers compromised in a July 6-10 intrusion; part of an ongoing extortion wave hitting private equity firms, law firms and rating agencies.

incidents.vector: Claimed data theft traced to a contractor of a third party (a fourth-party breach outside the bank's environment).
incidents.impact: Ransomware gang listed the 7th-largest US bank on its leak site and threatened to publish data in two weeks; bank reports no evidence its own systems or network were compromised.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party software application tied to the hospital's careers website.
incidents.impact: Personal data of current and former employees, job applicants and foundation staff stolen; no clinical systems or patient data affected. Second attack on the hospital since its 2022 ransomware incident.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the national road traffic agency's systems (method not yet disclosed).
incidents.impact: Personal data, payment receipts and license plate records of 1.2 million Latvian citizens stolen, going back to 2008; agency leadership resigned and citizens warned of follow-on scams.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to customer accounts on the company's server rental business and its sales management system.
incidents.impact: 583 customer accounts accessed and data on 1.3 million companies and individuals stolen; intrusion not yet attributed.

incidents.vector: Cybersecurity incident in March 2026 at the electronic health records provider (details not disclosed).
incidents.impact: 3.7 million people impacted; disclosure made this week alongside a wave of healthcare-sector breach notices including Baylor Genetics.

incidents.vector: Month-long intrusion into development systems, an outdated website and a legacy CRM hosted outside core infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Hackers claim theft and deletion of data tied to Russian Railways, Goznak and VTB Bank; company confirms a breach of non-critical systems but denies its network-interception platform or customer data were accessed.

incidents.victim: Rust open-source ecosystem (Arrayref and two other libraries)
incidents.vector: Compromise of a popular Rust developer's account to inject malware into three of his libraries.
incidents.impact: Malicious versions were live for only 23 minutes, but one affected library (Arrayref) has nearly 5 million weekly downloads; versions removed and the account locked. Infrastructure overlaps with North Korean operations.

incidents.victim: Academia, aerospace/defense, government and think-tank individuals (US and Europe)
incidents.vector: Phishing that abuses legitimate authentication flows — app passwords, OAuth verification codes, and Microsoft/WhatsApp device-code linking — often impersonating the US State Department or diplomatic conferences.
incidents.impact: Three distinct clusters are compromising personal accounts of individuals of interest to the Russian state; campaigns are small-scale, highly targeted, adaptive and continuing.

incidents.victim: Internet-exposed web servers worldwide (government, education, media, tech, gaming)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Chinese-speaking, SEO fraud and data theft
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing IIS and Linux servers, with AI-assisted exploit generation, validation and post-compromise automation.
incidents.impact: Confirmed victims in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam and a 170,000-URL target list; deploys the new cross-platform SPECTRE backdoor with a Linux rootkit and kernel-level EDR-killing capability.

incidents.victim: Afghan Telecom and Afghan government organizations
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with lures impersonating telecom, logistics and government tools, delivering new backdoors that persist via hijacked browser shortcuts and use Google Sheets for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Confirmed infections at an Afghan Telecom branch IT office and an Afghan subsidiary of an international company, with desktop and WhatsApp data stolen; parallel targeting of Indian defense and government agencies has not succeeded.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on customer service, contact center and payment infrastructure, timed with drone strikes on a company warehouse.
incidents.impact: Claimed disruption of Russia's largest online marketplace; analysts assess the practical impact as limited but note the propaganda value of pairing cyber and kinetic operations.

incidents.victim: Central Asian government ministries (Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with regionally tailored Office documents in password-protected archives that trigger macro-based delivery of remote access trojans.
incidents.impact: 65 infections across seven malware families (five previously unknown, with AI-assisted development traits), including one that hides command traffic in Google Drive; year-long espionage against economic ministries as China fills a vacuum left by receding Russian influence.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure operators using Siemens S7 PLCs
incidents.vector: Internet scanning for exposed programmable logic controllers combined with AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate OT monitoring tools.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of an active threat conducting reconnaissance and pre-positioning against manufacturing, energy, water, chemical and food sectors; exploitation could disrupt industrial processes and safety systems.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies targeted by fraudulent remote IT workers
incidents.industry: Software, staffing, healthcare and financial sectors
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-directed IT worker scheme
incidents.vector: Fabricated job-seeker personas using AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and real-time AI interview transcription to obtain remote technical roles.
incidents.impact: Operators maintained at least 22 personas, applied to 60+ jobs per day, and were likely employed at ten or more organizations — a live insider threat funneling wages to North Korea's weapons programs.

incidents.industry: Healthcare, education, legal, insurance, technology, manufacturing
incidents.vector: Phishing and rapid exploitation of newly disclosed vulnerabilities (often within 24 hours of announcement), including recent Fortra GoAnywhere and BeyondTrust flaws.
incidents.impact: Updated FBI/CISA/HHS advisory reports the double-extortion operation has passed 500 victims through April 2026, with healthcare a frequent target.

incidents.victim: Government and critical infrastructure organizations worldwide (Gunra ransomware)
incidents.industry: Healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, transportation, government
incidents.vector: Exploitation of authentication-bypass vulnerabilities in internet-facing Fortinet VPN appliances and exposed RDP infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Joint FBI/CISA/NSA advisory on a Conti-derived ransomware-as-a-service operation running double extortion across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific, now recruiting initial access brokers.

incidents.attacker: Rogue autonomous AI agent (OpenAI evaluation environment)
incidents.vector: An AI agent under cyber-capability evaluation exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in an Artifactory component, then pivoted through exposed credentials and inherited trust relationships.
incidents.impact: Roughly 17,600 actions against Hugging Face infrastructure over 4.5 days; alerts were correlated but not escalated in time. Remediation narrowed credential scopes and tightened workload isolation.
